description.para: Register offsets for the UART.
The Control register (CR) controls the major functions of the device.
Control Register Bit Definition
The mode register (MR) defines the mode of transfer as well as the data format.
If this register is modified during transmission or reception, data validity cannot be guaranteed.
Mode Register Bit Definition
Interrupt control logic uses the interrupt enable register (IER) and the interrupt disable register (IDR) to set the value of the bits in the interrupt mask register (IMR).

The IMR determines whether to pass an interrupt to the interrupt status register (ISR). Writing a 1 to IER enables an interrupt, writing a 1 to IDR disables an interrupt. IMR and ISR are read only, and IER and IDR are write only. Reading either IER or IDR returns 0x00.
All four registers have the same bit definitions.
The baud rate generator control register (BRGR) is a 16 bit register that controls the receiver bit sample clock and baud rate.
Valid values are 1 - 65535.
Bit Sample Rate = CCLK / BRGR, where the CCLK is selected by the MR_CCLK bit in the MR register.
The baud rate divider register (BDIV) controls how much the bit sample rate is divided by.
It sets the baud rate. Valid values are 0x04 to 0xFF. Writing a value less than 4 is ignored.
Baud rate = CCLK / ((BAUDDIV + 1) x BRGR), where the CCLK is selected by the MR_CCLK bit in the MR register.
Use the receiver timeout register (RTR) to detect an idle condition on the receiver data line.
Use the Receiver FIFO Trigger Level Register (RTRIG) to set the value at which the RX FIFO triggers an interrupt event.
Use the Transmit FIFO Trigger Level Register (TTRIG) to set the value at which the TX FIFO triggers an interrupt event.
This register (MODEMCR) controls the interface with the modem or data set, or a peripheral device emulating a modem.
This register (MODEMSR) indicates the current state of the control lines from a modem, or another peripheral device, to the CPU.
In addition, four bits of the modem status register provide change information. These bits are set to a logic 1 whenever a control input from the modem changes state.
Note: Whenever the DCTS, DDSR, TERI, or DDCD bit is set to logic 1, a modem status interrupt is generated and this is reflected in the modem status register.

The channel status register (CSR) is provided to enable the control logic to monitor the status of bits in the channel interrupt status register, even if these are masked out by the interrupt mask register.

briefdescription.para: RX FIFO fill over flow delay.

description.para: Operation of the flow delay register (FLOWDEL) is very similar to the receive FIFO trigger register.

An internal trigger signal activates when the FIFO is filled to the level set by this register. This trigger does not cause an interrupt, although it can be read through the channel status register. In hardware flow control mode, RTS is deactivated when the trigger becomes active. RTS only resets when the FIFO level is four less than the level of the flow delay trigger and the flow delay trigger is not activated. A value less than 4 disables the flow delay.
The Receiver FIFO Status register is used to have a continuous monitoring of the raw unmasked byte status information.
The register contains frame, parity and break status information for the top four bytes in the RX FIFO.
Receiver FIFO Byte Status Register Bit Definition

briefdescription.para: Sends the previously specified buffer from the instance variables.

detaileddescription.para: This is an internal function for the XUartPs driver that may be called from a shell function that sets up the buffer or from an interrupt handler.
Sends the specified buffer in either polled or interrupt driven modes. This function is non-blocking.
In polled mode, this function only sends as much data as the TX FIFO can buffer. The application may need to call it repeatedly to send the entire buffer.

In interrupt mode, this function starts the sending of the buffer. If not the entire buffer has been sent, then the interrupt handler continues the sending until the entire buffer has been sent. A callback function, as specified by the application, is called to indicate the completion of sending.

simplesect.para: The number of bytes actually sent.

briefdescription.para: Receives the previously specified buffer from the instance variables.

detaileddescription.para: This is an internal function that may be called from a shell function that sets up the buffer or from an interrupt handler.
Attempts to receive a specified number of bytes from the device and store them into the specified buffer. Works for either polled or interrupt driven modes. This function is non-blocking.

In polled mode, this function only receives as much data as in the RX FIFO. The application may need to call it repeatedly to receive the entire buffer. Polled mode is the default mode for the driver.

In interrupt mode, this function starts the receiving. If not the entire buffer has been received, the interrupt handler continues until the entire buffer has been received. A callback function, as specified by the application, is called to indicate the completion of the receiving or error conditions.

simplesect.para: The number of bytes received.

The baud rate is set to a default value specified by Config->DefaultBaudRate if set, otherwise it is set to 19.2K baud. The receive FIFO threshold is set for 8 bytes. The default operating mode of the driver is polled mode.

The caller is responsible for keeping the address mapping from EffectiveAddr to the device physical base address unchanged once this function is invoked. Unexpected errors may occur if the address mapping changes after this function is called. If address translation is not used, pass in the physical address instead.

XST_UART_BAUD_ERROR if the baud rate is not possible because the inputclock frequency is not divisible with an acceptable amount of error.

briefdescription.para: Sends the specified buffer in polled or interrupt driven mode.

detaileddescription.para: This function is non-blocking. If the device is busy sending data, it returns and indicates zero bytes were sent. Otherwise, it fills the TX FIFO as much as it can, and returns the number of bytes sent.
In polled mode, this function only sends as much data as the TX FIFO can buffer. The application may need to call it repeatedly to send the entire buffer.

In interrupt mode, this function starts sending the specified buffer, then the interrupt handler continues sending data until the entire buffer has been sent. A callback function, as specified by the application, is called to indicate the completion of sending.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to a buffer of data to send.
Number of bytes to send. A value of zero stops a previous send operation that is in progress in interrupt mode. Any data that was already put into the transmit FIFO is sent.

simplesect.para: The number of bytes actually sent.
The number of bytes is not asserted so that this function may be called with a value of zero to stop an operation that is already in progress.

briefdescription.para: Receives a specified number of bytes of data from the device.

detaileddescription.para: Attempts to receive data and store it into the specified buffer. Works for both polled or interrupt driven modes. This function is non-blocking.

In polled mode, this function only receives the data already in the RX FIFO. The application may need to call it repeatedly to receive the entire buffer. Polled mode is the default mode of operation for the device.

In interrupt mode, this function starts the receiving. If not the entire buffer has been received, the interrupt handler continues receiving data until the entire buffer has been received. A callback function, as specified by the application, is called to indicate the completion of the receiving or error conditions.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to buffer to receive data into.
Number of bytes to receive. A value of zero stops a previous receive operation that is in progress in interrupt mode.

simplesect.para: The number of bytes received.
The number of bytes is not asserted so that this function may be called with a value of zero to stop an operation that is already in progress.

briefdescription.para: Number of entries in the options table.
Provides the driver interface for the XUartPs UART device.

detaileddescription.para: This driver supports the following features:

listitem.para: Dynamic data format (baud rate, data bits, stop bits, parity)
Polled mode
Interrupt driven mode
Transmit and receive FIFOs (32 byte FIFO depth)
Access to the external modem control lines

detaileddescription.para: The XUartPs_Config structure is used by the driver to configure itself. Fields inside this structure are properties of XUartPs based on its hardware build.
To support multiple runtime loading and initialization strategies employed by various operating systems, the driver instance can be initialized in the following way:

listitem.para: XUartPs_CfgInitialize(InstancePtr, CfgPtr, EffectiveAddr) - Uses a configuration structure provided by the caller. If running in a system with address translation, the parameter EffectiveAddr should be the virtual address.

detaileddescription.para: The UART has an internal baud rate generator, which furnishes the baud rate clock for both the receiver and the transmitter. The input clock frequency can be either the master clock or the master clock divided by 8, configured through the mode register.

Accompanied with the baud rate divider register, the baud rate is determined by: baud_rate = input_clock / (bgen * (bdiv + 1) where bgen is the value of the baud rate generator, and bdiv is the value of baud rate divider.
The FIFOs are not flushed when the driver is initialized, but a function is provided to allow resetting the FIFOs if desired.
The driver defaults to no interrupts at initialization such that interrupts must be enabled if desired. An interrupt is generated for one of the following conditions.

listitem.para: A change in the modem signals
Data in the receive FIFO for a configurable time without receiver activity
A parity error
A framing error
An overrun error
Transmit FIFO is full
Transmit FIFO is empty
Receive FIFO is full
Receive FIFO is empty
Data in the receive FIFO equal to the receive threshold

detaileddescription.para: The application can control which interrupts are enabled using the XUartPs_SetInterruptMask() function.

To use interrupts, connect the driver interrupt handler, XUartPs_InterruptHandler(), to the interrupt system of the application. A separate handler should be provided by the application to communicate with the interrupt system, and conduct application specific interrupt handling. An application registers its own handler through the XUartPs_SetHandler() function.
The functions, XUartPs_Send() and XUartPs_Recv(), are provided in the driver to allow data to be sent and received. They can be used in either polled or interrupt mode.

simplesect.para: The default configuration for the UART after initialization is:

listitem.para: 9,600 bps or XPAR_DFT_BAUDRATE if defined
8 data bits
1 stop bit
no parity
FIFO's are enabled with a receive threshold of 8 bytes
The RX timeout is enabled with a timeout of 1 (4 char times)
